name: Physical Infrastructure and Property
blurb: Property cover on the buildings themselves. Liquid cooling leaks, transformer and substation failures under sudden AI load, battery storage fire risk, structural floor loading on racks above 100 kW, water use and environmental impairment, small modular reactor co-location, physical sabotage, and how reinsurers price site selection.

reading.body:
Liquid-related damage is close to a quarter of data centre loss costs, and AI's physical footprint concentrates the remaining property risk in power failures, battery fires, and site exposure rather than servers.

The pattern is that AI-specific infrastructure changes the physical risk before the insurance market fully catches up. Direct-to-chip cooling puts fluid next to energised equipment, and FM added a liquid-cooling section to its 2026 loss prevention guidance only after the exposure existed. Sudden AI workload spikes overheat substations and transformers, and racks above 100 kW force structural retrofits that property policies must now address.

Site selection is becoming an underwriting decision as much as an engineering one. Reinsurers price seismic, coastal surge and grid vulnerability by geography, and wildfire or flood exposure leads to premium increases or refusals. Drone strikes on three AWS facilities in the UAE and Bahrain in March 2026 moved geopolitical exclusion review from theoretical to live for Gulf-region operators, and the same wording reaches any site near contested airspace.

The data does not quantify premium levels, total losses beyond the liquid-cooling share, or how often the other nine risks occur. It also does not separate new-build from retrofit exposure, but the list includes both retrofitting legacy buildings and co-locating micro reactors.

summary: Property cover on the buildings themselves. Liquid cooling leaks, transformer and substation failures under sudden AI load, battery storage fire risk, structural floor loading on racks above 100 kW, water use and environmental impairment, small modular reactor co-location, physical sabotage, and how reinsurers price site selection.
